params.question: Which of the following deaths would NOT be classified as a maternal death under the WHO definition?

answers.text: A woman dying of eclampsia 30 days after delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Eclampsia is a direct obstetric cause, and death within 42 days of delivery from a pregnancy-related complication meets the WHO definition of a maternal death.

answers.text: A woman with rheumatic heart disease dying 20 days after caesarean section

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is an indirect obstetric death. Rheumatic heart disease is a pre-existing condition aggravated by the physiological burden of pregnancy, so it fits the WHO definition.

answers.text: A pregnant woman dying in a road traffic accident at 36 weeks of gestation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A road traffic accident is an accidental cause unrelated to the pregnancy or its management. The WHO definition explicitly excludes deaths from accidental or incidental causes, even if the woman is pregnant.

answers.text: A woman dying of puerperal sepsis 10 days after delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Puerperal sepsis is a direct obstetric complication. Death within 42 days from this cause clearly qualifies as a maternal death under the WHO definition.

overallFeedback.feedback: The WHO definition of maternal death specifically excludes accidental or incidental causes. A road traffic accident — regardless of the woman's pregnancy status — is not related to the pregnancy itself and is therefore not counted as a maternal death.

Correct. The WHO definition of maternal death excludes deaths from accidental or incidental causes, even if the woman is pregnant. Only deaths related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management qualify.

params.question: A fresh (intrapartum) stillbirth typically shows skin desquamation, greenish discolouration, and collapsed tissues.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: These features describe a macerated stillbirth, not a fresh one. Desquamation, greenish discolouration, and collapsed tissues indicate the foetus died well before delivery. A fresh (intrapartum) stillbirth shows no signs of maceration, meaning death occurred near the time of delivery — and many such deaths are preventable.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. These features — skin peeling, discolouration, and tissue softening — are hallmarks of a macerated stillbirth, where the foetus died in the womb hours to days before delivery. A fresh stillbirth shows no maceration, indicating death occurred close to delivery, often from acute events like cord prolapse or placental abruption.

params.question: A district hospital's caesarean section rate is 32%, well above the WHO benchmark of 10–15%. What is the primary purpose of conducting a structured caesarean audit at this facility?

answers.text: To penalise individual obstetricians who perform caesarean sections beyond the benchmark

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Caesarean audit is a quality improvement tool, not a punitive measure. Its goal is to understand delivery patterns across patient groups, not to assign blame to individual clinicians.

answers.text: To ban all elective caesarean sections until the rate drops below 15 per cent

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Audit aims to understand and improve practice, not to impose blanket restrictions. Some elective caesareans are clinically necessary and appropriate.

answers.text: To identify which patient subgroups are driving the high rate and determine whether it reflects genuine clinical need

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Caesarean audit classifies every delivery to reveal which patient groups — such as women with a previous caesarean, induced nulliparous women, or preterm cases — contribute most to the rate, and whether clinical indications justify those caesareans.

answers.text: To calculate the facility's maternal mortality ratio for national reporting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The maternal mortality ratio uses maternal deaths and live births as its inputs. Caesarean audit focuses specifically on the caesarean rate and its clinical appropriateness — a separate quality metric.

overallFeedback.feedback: The primary purpose of caesarean audit is quality improvement — identifying which patient subgroups (e.g. women with a prior caesarean, induced nulliparous women) drive the rate, and determining whether it reflects genuine clinical need or other pressures like litigation fear or staffing gaps.
Correct. Caesarean audit examines which patient groups contribute to the rate and whether those caesareans were clinically justified, guiding targeted interventions rather than blanket restrictions.

interactions.label: How do Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)

params.question: How do Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) differ in their approach to promoting institutional deliveries?

answers.text: JSY provides free hospital services, while JSSK provides a conditional cash transfer to eligible women

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This reverses the two schemes. JSY is the conditional cash transfer programme (launched 2005), while JSSK (launched 2011) eliminates out-of-pocket costs by providing free services at the facility.

answers.text: JSY covers only urban women, while JSSK covers only rural women

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both schemes cover rural and urban women. In low-performing states, JSY covers all pregnant women regardless of income or area. JSSK applies to all government facility deliveries.

answers.text: JSY guarantees respectful maternity care, while JSSK provides iron and folic acid supplementation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Respectful maternity care is guaranteed under SUMAN (2019), not JSY. Iron and folic acid supplementation falls under Anaemia Mukt Bharat (2018), not JSSK.

answers.text: JSY provides a conditional cash transfer to encourage facility delivery, while JSSK eliminates out-of-pocket costs for delivery and newborn care

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: JSY (2005) incentivises women to choose institutional delivery through direct cash payments. JSSK (2011) removes the financial barrier at the facility — free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood transfusions, meals, and transport for mothers and sick newborns.

overallFeedback.feedback: JSY (2005) is a conditional cash transfer that incentivises institutional delivery. JSSK (2011) removes costs at the facility entirely — free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood transfusions, meals, and transport. Together they tackle different barriers: the decision to seek facility care (JSY) and the cost of receiving it (JSSK).

Correct. JSY and JSSK are complementary. JSY encourages women to choose a facility through cash incentives, while JSSK ensures no out-of-pocket expense once they arrive — covering delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, meals, and transport.

interactions.label: A woman with severe anaemia arrives in labour at your government district hospit

params.question: A woman with severe anaemia arrives in labour at your government district hospital and delivers by emergency caesarean section. As the attending medical officer, which of the following actions correctly applies your clinical responsibilities?

answers.text: Discharge her after delivery without screening for scheme eligibility, since programme enrolment is handled by the ASHA worker at the community level

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Programme eligibility screening is a clinical responsibility at the point of care. The attending medical officer must identify entitlements under JSSK, SUMAN, and Anaemia Mukt Bharat — this cannot be deferred to the community level.

answers.text: Register the birth within twenty-four hours, screen her entitlements under JSSK and SUMAN, classify the delivery in a Robson group, and escalate her anaemia management under Anaemia Mukt Bharat protocols

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This integrates all four domains of clinical responsibility: timely birth registration (legal requirement), programme enrolment (entitlement screening), prospective Robson classification for audit, and protocol-based management.

answers.text: Refer her to a private hospital for blood transfusion, since government facilities do not provide this service free of cost

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Under JSSK, blood transfusions during delivery are provided free at government facilities. Referring her to a private hospital contradicts the programme guarantee and delays care.

answers.text: Classify the delivery under the Robson system only if the caesarean was planned before labour, since Robson grouping does not apply to emergency procedures

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Robson classification covers every obstetric patient — whether vaginal, elective caesarean, or emergency caesarean. The onset-of-labour variable (spontaneous, induced, or pre-labour caesarean) is one of six recorded elements, and all values are valid Robson groups.

overallFeedback.feedback: As the attending medical officer, you must register every birth within twenty-four hours, screen each woman's entitlements under JSSK, SUMAN, and Anaemia Mukt Bharat, assign a Robson group at discharge regardless of mode of delivery, and participate in audit. These are clinical responsibilities at the point of care.

Correct. Your responsibilities as the attending medical officer include registering every birth within twenty-four hours, screening for national programme entitlements, classifying every delivery in a Robson group at discharge, and participating in clinical audit — these are clinical duties, not administrative formalities.
